newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish Agency welcomes Swiss Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Jewish Agency welcomes Swiss Holocaust fund.

text.p: A Jewish group campaigning to recover money left in Swiss banks by Jewish victims of World War Two welcomed a Swiss decision on Wednesday to create a Holocaust memorial fund but stressed the action was a stopgap measure.
"It is a great achievment," Jewish Agency Chairman Avraham Burg said through his spokeswoman.

"The decision indicated goodwill but is not a solution to the problem. The only solution will be when all assets looted from the Jews will be returned to Jewish hands," the spokeswoman quoted Burg as saying.
Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti said on Wednesday Switzerland would create a memorial fund that taps contributions from banks and other businesses to aid victims of the Holocaust.

But he rebuffed calls for a quick decision on what payment Switzerland would make, saying Berne had to await the findings of a historians' panel examining Switzerland's role as a World War Two financial centre.

Under international pressure, the three largest Swiss banks last week agreed to put up 100 million Swiss francs ($70 million) to aid Holocaust victims and their families. Other businesses pledged to follow suit.
Berne is coordinating the fund, which aims to assure critics that the Swiss are taking seriously allegations they profited from World War Two and banks kept the wealth of victims of Nazi Germany.
"From our point of view, no one is doing us a favour. This is not Swiss money, It belongs to the Jews," Burg said.
A commission including Swiss and U.S. bankers as well as Jewish representatives is investigating the accounts in Swiss banks. Six million Jews were killed in the Holocaust.
